The main takeaway from our work is that

the mouse receptor displays a remarkable selectivity for the primary ammonium ions, and that the selectivity of mouse receptor for organic cations is different from the selectivity of other nicotinic receptors.

the selectivity of a channel for a given ion is determined by the sum of the effects of many amino acid side chains and that a change in the permeability ratio of one cation to another is not a reliable guide to the effect of a mutation on the selectivity for a third cation.
M2 plays a critical role in determining ion selectivity of the nicotinic acetyicholine receptor.
